_comment: Approved permissions and exported components of the release merged manifest. Add an entry only with the task or store-checklist row that justifies it (docs/store/READINESS.md). ${applicationId} stands for the application id. "uri-grant-providers" lists every content provider with grantUriPermissions=true by authority; each must be not exported.

uses-permission.android.permission.INTERNET: Mail sync: the Rust core opens its own TLS connections to the person's IMAP and SMTP servers (docs/store/READINESS.md, permissions table; T16).
uses-permission.android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE: The connectivity callback (ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback) that tells the core whether the device has a network, so that the Offline banner is true and nothing is sent while offline (T16). Normal permission, no data leaves the device.
uses-permission.android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS: T20, S32: new-mail notifications. Runtime permission on Android 13 and later, asked only from S07 after the first account; the app works fully without it (docs/store/READINESS.md, permissions table).
uses-permission.android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETE: Merged by WorkManager (T20): it restores the periodic check's schedule after a restart (its RescheduleReceiver). Croft has no boot receiver of its own. Normal permission (docs/store/READINESS.md, permissions table).
uses-permission.android.permission.WAKE_LOCK: Merged by WorkManager (T20): held by WorkManager while the periodic check runs. Normal permission, no data leaves the device.
uses-permission.${applicationId}.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EX: AndroidX core adds this signature-level permission (declared by the app itself, protectionLevel signature) so that dynamically registered receivers are not exported; not grantable to other apps.

permission.${applicationId}.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EX: The declaration paired with the uses-permission above; must stay protectionLevel=signature.

activity:${namespace}.MainActivity.why: The launcher activity, and the entry for mailto: links and shares (T18d, S23): VIEW and SENDTO with a mailto: URI, SEND and SEND_MULTIPLE with text and content: streams. They only fill the compose screen; nothing is sent without Send.

receiver:androidx.profileinstaller.Profi.why: AndroidX profileinstaller (baseline profiles): lets the shell trigger profile installation. Only the system or adb can hold android.permission.DUMP, so other apps cannot call it.

service:androidx.work.impl.background.sy.why: WorkManager (T20): the JobScheduler service that runs the periodic check. Only the system can bind it (android.permission.BIND_JOB_SERVICE).

receiver:androidx.work.impl.diagnostics..why: WorkManager (T20): lets the shell ask for WorkManager's diagnostics in the log. Only the system or adb can hold android.permission.DUMP, so other apps cannot call it.

activity:${namespace}.CompanionRedirectA.why: T34b, S06: the end of signing in to the person's Croft Companion through the browser (RFC 8252). The Companion's sign-in page sends the browser to ${applicationId}:/companion?code=...; this activity hands that address to the core and closes. It acts only while a sign-in the person started in the app is waiting (anything else is ignored), and the code is useless without the PKCE verifier the core keeps.

${applicationId}.attachments.why: T18b (S21): the FileProvider that gives a viewer app read access to one attachment the person opened, with a temporary URI grant (FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION). Not exported. Its paths file (res/xml/shared_attachment_paths.xml) exposes only cacheDir/shared-attachments/; a test asserts that. Compose refuses content: URIs of this authority as share input.

_stores_comment: Entries that only one store build may have (T34d), keyed by store; a key may name several stores, comma-separated. tools/check-release-manifest.py adds the entries of the store named by CROFT_STORE (set by check-release-outputs.sh) to the common ones above.

uses-permission.com.google.android.c2dm.permission.RECEI: T34d, play: Firebase Cloud Messaging. Lets Google Play services deliver the push gateway's pings (content-free) to the app. Normal permission.

receiver:com.google.firebase.iid.Firebas.why: T34d, play: Firebase Cloud Messaging's receiver. Only Google Play services holds com.google.android.c2dm.permission.SEND, so no other app can deliver to it.

receiver:org.unifiedpush.android.connect.why: T34d, fdroid and github: UnifiedPush's connector library. The distributor app (ntfy, for example) delivers new endpoints and messages to this receiver by broadcast; the library acts only on broadcasts carrying the random token of this app's own registration (anything else is dropped), and Croft counts a message only when it decrypted with this device's Web Push keys. Messages only make the app check for mail.

service:org.unifiedpush.android.connecto.why: T34d, fdroid and github: UnifiedPush's connector library. A distributor binds it for a few seconds with foreground importance so the app may run its check (the UnifiedPush specification). The binder does nothing; no foreground service is started by Croft.
